record_type_quote: To assess the reproducibility and external validity of these results, we conducted an independent replication using long-term data from a clinical trial cohort.

targets.authors: Cortese M, Peng X, Edan G, Freedman MS, Hartung HP, Montalban X
targets.title: Serum alpha-linolenic acid and long-term multiple sclerosis activity and progression
targets.outcome_quote: More specifically, our findings replicate the reported associations between ALA and lower disability as well as preserved brain structure. The consistency across independent cohorts strengthens the notion that ALA may play a protective role in MS-related neurodegeneration. However, several discrepancies also emerged. We found a positive association between ALA and T2-weighted lesion counts at baseline in multivariable models.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The discussion confirms particular associations but explicitly frames the replication as also having discrepancies, including a lesion-count association not observed in the original. The favorable summary of disability and brain-volume associations is narrower than an overall verdict covering all tested findings. Earlier analyses of the reused cohort supply data and contextual comparisons rather than additional designed replication targets.
